claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the driver drove 12.4 km against a 10.8 km optimal route, +1.6 km (+15%), and the whole excess is concentrated in one off-route segment at 22:57–23:01 where he drove 2.19 km over ground the optimal route covers in 1.38 km, adding 0.80 km and straying up to 1014 m from the optimal route.

Nothing in the chat shows any route change agreed with the rider: the only messages are the rider's pickup note and the driver's arrival text (22:45, 22:46), and the driver's own statement that he 'went round' AJE is an after-the-fact explanation, not prior consent.

The driver's congestion excuse fails the policy's evidentiary test: there is no traffic incident recorded near the route during the trip window, and the only congestion supporting him (AJE band 1) is a band fact that cannot by itself justify a reroute under the MVP rule.

Because this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, the unexempted 0.80 km off-route segment was billed at the metered per-km rate of $1.41/km, so the rider is owed $1.13 (0.80 km × $1.41), derived from the fare's own distance rate.

The refund should be limited to the mileage unit of the unexempted segment ($1.13) and should not extend to the residual map-matching difference between the total billed excess ($2.33 for 1.6 km) and the segment sum, which the policy leaves with the fare.
No additional waiting or extra published surcharge is claimed: the fare breakdown shows $0.00 waiting fee and no undocumented add-on beyond base, distance, time and platform fee.
RydeTAXI does not support app-based destination changes, so the only way the detour could have been legitimate was a chat agreement reached before the driver left the optimal route — and none exists.
The driver has 729 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes upheld, so the repeated-breach account flag is not warranted here; this brief seeks only the rider's mileage refund.

weaknesses: The driver will cite F10 (AJE speed band 1, 0–9 km/h, 22:39–22:57) plus F14 (light rain, 1.8 mm) as 'reasonable cause' for avoiding the expressway, and F2 shows only +4.3 min, which he will argue a detour saved rather than cost him.

The off-route segment (F3) at 22:57–23:01 begins as the recorded AJE band-1 window closes, so the judge may read the timing as coincidental with real congestion even though F13 records no incident on the optimal route.

The billed excess the rider complains about is larger than my claim: F4 shows $2.33 for 1.6 km, but RD-2 confines any refund to the 0.80 km segment sum ($1.13), so I cannot recover the full $2.33 and my own claim admits the shortfall.

The rider's own profile (F15) shows 3 disputes in 90 days with only 1 upheld, which the driver may use to characterise this complaint as another unmeritorious fare challenge; profile facts cannot decide the case but can colour it.

claims.assertion: The trip was a RydeTAXI metered trip (total charged $28.48 SGD made up of base, distance, time and platform components), so the rider's complaint is governed by the metered-fare branch of the policy, not the flat-quote branch.

The GPS record shows only ONE off-route segment (22:57–23:01), of 2.19 km driven against 1.38 km on the optimal route, i.e. 0.80 km of extra distance — not the 1.6 km the rider claims — so the maximum distance exposed to any refund is 0.80 km.

That off-route segment was driven while Ayer Rajah Expressway (category 1) was recorded at the worst speed band, band 1 (0–9 km/h), during 22:39–22:57, immediately before the deviation began at 22:57.

The congestion evidence is on the substituted portion of the optimal route: the AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY band-1 record is category-1 Expressway data matching the optimal route corridor that the driver bypassed, and the driver's reroute is corroborated by the same-band condition on the parallel CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY (F11) and the merely band-4 (30–39 km/h) condition on Kent Ridge Road (F12), plus light rain (F14).

The driver's account of the reason for the detour is recorded in the driver statement, and it is consistent with the LTA speed-band records rather than contradicted by them; the deviation was short-lived (4 minutes of a 21.6-minute trip).

The rider never proposed or approved a route; the chat contains only pickup-location messages, and no agreement to a specific route was given before the deviation, so the rider's non-consent is not in dispute — the only question is whether the deviation had a reasonable cause.

The driver's record shows 0 of 2 disputes upheld in 90 days and a 4.8 rating over 729 trips, so no repeated route violation exists to support any account flag; the rider, by contrast, has 3 disputes in 90 days, 1 upheld.

Because no unstructured item was added to the metered fare (waiting $0.00, no extra fees, no surge), and the fare was computed from the metered distance and time, no FARE-1 style unauthorised add-on exists to refund; any adjustment can only be the RD-2 mileage unit for an unexempted segment.

weaknesses: F13 records NO traffic incidents near the route during the trip window, so there is no traffic-incident-* corroboration — under RD-4(a) the segment can only be reasoned through the speed-band record, and RD-4(b) says a speed-band record alone is not sufficient for exemption in the MVP (open gap G3).

The Ayer Rajah Expressway band-1 record runs 22:39–22:57 while the off-route segment only starts at 22:57, so the rider will argue the congestion had ended exactly when the driver deviated and that the band record is not on the substituted optimal route portion.

The rider will rely on F1 (actual 12.4 km vs 10.8 km optimal, +1.6 km) and F4 ($2.33 excess distance billed) to ask for the full excess, and on F3's 'up to 1014 m from the optimal route' maximum deviation to argue this was a genuine detour, not noise.
No chat message records the driver telling the rider about the reroute before or during it, so RD-5 consent cannot be claimed and the driver is confined to the RD-4 reasonable-cause defence.

The 4.3-minute excess duration (F2) against a 1.6 km excess may be used to argue the deviation was not simply congestion avoidance; only the metered distance delta is refundable under RD-2, which may not satisfy the rider.

events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 9 points
events.body:
→ D1 (concedes): Conceded — F6 confirms a RydeTAXI metered fare ($3.90 base, $17.50 distance for 12.4 km, $5.61 time, $1.47 platform), so only the RD-2 metered branch applies; that branch is exactly what yields my $1.13 claim, not a bar to it. [F6] [RD-2]
→ D2 (concedes): Agreed on the arithmetic and it is my own position: F3 fixes the off-route segment at +0.80 km, so 0.80 km is the maximum refundable distance, and F4's $2.33 figure for the full 1.6 km excess is not what I claim under RD-2. [F3 F4 F1] [RD-2]
→ D3: The band-1 AJE record runs 22:39–22:57 (F10) while the off-route segment only begins at 22:57 (F3), so by the driver's own timeline the congestion window closed exactly as he deviated; a condition that had already ended cannot be the reasonable cause for the deviation, and RD-4(b) makes a speed band alone insufficient anyway. [F10 F3] [RD-4]
→ D4: RD-4 requires traffic corroboration aimed at the substituted portion of the optimal route, and F13 records no traffic incident near the route during the trip window; F11 and F12 are records on other corridors and F14 is light rain, none of which is an incident on the replaced optimal route as RD-4(a) demands. [F11 F12 F13 F14] [RD-4]
→ D5: The driver's statement (F9) is user-submitted content and loses to the system records: F13 shows no incident and F10's congestion window ended at 22:57, so F9 is not corroborated; F2's +4.3 min and F3's 1014 m maximum stray are consistent with a detour that cost time rather than avoided it. [F9 F10 F13 F2 F3] [RD-4]
→ D6: The driver concedes there was no route agreement, and RD-5 requires the rider's consent to have been given before the driver left the optimal route — none exists in F7/F8, so the segment stands unexempted and RD-1/RD-2 apply. [F7 F8 F3] [RD-5 RD-1 RD-2]
→ D7 (concedes): I agree no account flag is warranted — F16 shows 0 of 2 disputes upheld over 729 trips and my claim is limited to the $1.13 mileage unit; F15 is rider profile data and cannot defeat a rider's substantive refund claim under RD-2. [F16 F15] [RD-6 RD-2]
→ D8 (concedes): Conceded on the FARE-1 point — F6 shows waiting $0.00 and F5 shows no surge, so there is no unauthorised add-on to strip out; my claim rests solely on the RD-2 metered mileage unit of the unexempted 0.80 km segment, i.e. 0.80 × $1.41 = $1.13. [F6 F5 F3 F4] [FARE-1 RD-2]
→ C1: My own case does not survive the RD-4(b) record fully intact: the driver is right that F10's band-1 reading is genuine congestion data on an expressway corridor and F14 (light rain) supports bad conditions at the time, so the judge may find a reasonable-cause gloss on the deviation even though F13 supplies no incident; I therefore keep the claim confined to the strict RD-2 mileage unit rather than the full $2.33 in F4. [F10 F14 F13 F4] [RD-4 RD-2]

→ C7: RD-3 governs passenger-requested stops and destination changes, and none is alleged here; the applicable provision is RD-4 reasonable cause, which is met by the expressway speed-band record at F10 with the parallel-route corroboration at F11 and F12. [F7 F8 F9 F10 F11 F12] [RD-3 RD-4 RD-5]

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $1.13 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
Route deviation on a metered RydeTAXI trip. The GPS record shows one off-route segment, 22:57–23:01, 2.19 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.38 km, adding 0.80 km [F3]; overall the trip ran 12.4 km against a 10.8 km optimal route (+1.6 km) [F1]. Under RD-1 that segment is an off-route segment and must be tested against RD-3, RD-4 and RD-5 before it counts as unexempted.

The rider never requested a stop or a destination change; the only chat is the rider's pickup note and the driver's arrival text [F7][F8], so no segment is exempted by RD-3, which governs rider-named stops (RydeTAXI also does not support app-based destination changes).

There was no route agreement before the deviation: the driver's statement that he "went round" AYE is an after-the-fact explanation [F9], and nothing in [F7][F8] shows the driver naming a route and the rider agreeing before he left the optimal route, so RD-5 exemption fails.

The reasonable-cause defence under RD-4 also fails. RD-4(a) requires a traffic-incident fact on the replaced optimal stretch reported before the detour and still listed during the trip window; [F13] records no incident near the route at all. The congestion material is band data only — AYE band 1 during 22:39–22:57 [F10], CE band 1 [F11], Kent Ridge Road band 4 [F12] — and RD-4(b) makes a speed band, on its own, insufficient for exemption (open gap G3); the MVP does not exempt on band data alone. Weather (light rain, 1.8 mm) [F14] is not one of RD-4's accepted corroborants. The band-1 window on AYE also closes at 22:57 [F10] exactly when the deviation begins [F3], so it does not even temporally cover the substituted stretch. The segment is therefore unexempted.

Amount (RydeTAXI branch of RD-2): refund = Σ extra_km of unexempted segments × per-km rate = distance_fare ÷ distance_km = $17.50 ÷ 12.4 km = $1.4113/km [F6]; 0.80 km × $1.4113/km = $1.129 ≈ $1.13 [F3][F4][F6]. The residual map-matching difference between the total billed excess ($2.33 for 1.6 km, [F4]) and the segment sum is expressly left with the fare under RD-2, so the refund is confined to $1.13.

No additional add-on is refundable: waiting $0.00, no surge, only base/distance/time plus the published platform fee [F5][F6], so FARE-1 exposes nothing. RD-6 flag_account is not triggered: the driver has 0 of 2 route disputes upheld in 90 days [F16], and the riding profile facts [F15][F16] are not used to decide the route question.

The driver's congestion excuse fails the policy's evidentiary test: there is no traffic incident recorded near the route during the trip window, and the only congestion supporting him (AJE band 1) is a band fact that cannot by itself justify a reroute under the MVP rule.

Because this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, the unexempted 0.80 km off-route segment was billed at the metered per-km rate of $1.41/km, so the rider is owed $1.13 (0.80 km × $1.41), derived from the fare's own distance rate.

The refund should be limited to the mileage unit of the unexempted segment ($1.13) and should not extend to the residual map-matching difference between the total billed excess ($2.33 for 1.6 km) and the segment sum, which the policy leaves with the fare.
No additional waiting or extra published surcharge is claimed: the fare breakdown shows $0.00 waiting fee and no undocumented add-on beyond base, distance, time and platform fee.

The off-route segment (F3) at 22:57–23:01 begins as the recorded AJE band-1 window closes, so the judge may read the timing as coincidental with real congestion even though F13 records no incident on the optimal route.

The billed excess the rider complains about is larger than my claim: F4 shows $2.33 for 1.6 km, but RD-2 confines any refund to the 0.80 km segment sum ($1.13), so I cannot recover the full $2.33 and my own claim admits the shortfall.

That off-route segment was driven while Ayer Rajah Expressway (category 1) was recorded at the worst speed band, band 1 (0–9 km/h), during 22:39–22:57, immediately before the deviation began at 22:57.

The congestion evidence is on the substituted portion of the optimal route: the AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY band-1 record is category-1 Expressway data matching the optimal route corridor that the driver bypassed, and the driver's reroute is corroborated by the same-band condition on the parallel CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY (F11) and the merely band-4 (30–39 km/h) condition on Kent Ridge Road (F12), plus light rain (F14).

The driver's account of the reason for the detour is recorded in the driver statement, and it is consistent with the LTA speed-band records rather than contradicted by them; the deviation was short-lived (4 minutes of a 21.6-minute trip).

The rider never proposed or approved a route; the chat contains only pickup-location messages, and no agreement to a specific route was given before the deviation, so the rider's non-consent is not in dispute — the only question is whether the deviation had a reasonable cause.

The driver's record shows 0 of 2 disputes upheld in 90 days and a 4.8 rating over 729 trips, so no repeated route violation exists to support any account flag; the rider, by contrast, has 3 disputes in 90 days, 1 upheld.

Because no unstructured item was added to the metered fare (waiting $0.00, no extra fees, no surge), and the fare was computed from the metered distance and time, no FARE-1 style unauthorised add-on exists to refund; any adjustment can only be the RD-2 mileage unit for an unexempted segment.

weaknesses: F13 records NO traffic incidents near the route during the trip window, so there is no traffic-incident-* corroboration — under RD-4(a) the segment can only be reasoned through the speed-band record, and RD-4(b) says a speed-band record alone is not sufficient for exemption in the MVP (open gap G3).

The Ayer Rajah Expressway band-1 record runs 22:39–22:57 while the off-route segment only starts at 22:57, so the rider will argue the congestion had ended exactly when the driver deviated and that the band record is not on the substituted optimal route portion.

The rider will rely on F1 (actual 12.4 km vs 10.8 km optimal, +1.6 km) and F4 ($2.33 excess distance billed) to ask for the full excess, and on F3's 'up to 1014 m from the optimal route' maximum deviation to argue this was a genuine detour, not noise.
No chat message records the driver telling the rider about the reroute before or during it, so RD-5 consent cannot be claimed and the driver is confined to the RD-4 reasonable-cause defence.

The 4.3-minute excess duration (F2) against a 1.6 km excess may be used to argue the deviation was not simply congestion avoidance; only the metered distance delta is refundable under RD-2, which may not satisfy the rider.

points.response: Conceded — F6 confirms a RydeTAXI metered fare ($3.90 base, $17.50 distance for 12.4 km, $5.61 time, $1.47 platform), so only the RD-2 metered branch applies; that branch is exactly what yields my $1.13 claim, not a bar to it.

Agreed on the arithmetic and it is my own position: F3 fixes the off-route segment at +0.80 km, so 0.80 km is the maximum refundable distance, and F4's $2.33 figure for the full 1.6 km excess is not what I claim under RD-2.

The band-1 AJE record runs 22:39–22:57 (F10) while the off-route segment only begins at 22:57 (F3), so by the driver's own timeline the congestion window closed exactly as he deviated; a condition that had already ended cannot be the reasonable cause for the deviation, and RD-4(b) makes a speed band alone insufficient anyway.

RD-4 requires traffic corroboration aimed at the substituted portion of the optimal route, and F13 records no traffic incident near the route during the trip window; F11 and F12 are records on other corridors and F14 is light rain, none of which is an incident on the replaced optimal route as RD-4(a) demands.

The driver's statement (F9) is user-submitted content and loses to the system records: F13 shows no incident and F10's congestion window ended at 22:57, so F9 is not corroborated; F2's +4.3 min and F3's 1014 m maximum stray are consistent with a detour that cost time rather than avoided it.

The driver concedes there was no route agreement, and RD-5 requires the rider's consent to have been given before the driver left the optimal route — none exists in F7/F8, so the segment stands unexempted and RD-1/RD-2 apply.

I agree no account flag is warranted — F16 shows 0 of 2 disputes upheld over 729 trips and my claim is limited to the $1.13 mileage unit; F15 is rider profile data and cannot defeat a rider's substantive refund claim under RD-2.

Conceded on the FARE-1 point — F6 shows waiting $0.00 and F5 shows no surge, so there is no unauthorised add-on to strip out; my claim rests solely on the RD-2 metered mileage unit of the unexempted 0.80 km segment, i.e. 0.80 × $1.41 = $1.13.

My own case does not survive the RD-4(b) record fully intact: the driver is right that F10's band-1 reading is genuine congestion data on an expressway corridor and F14 (light rain) supports bad conditions at the time, so the judge may find a reasonable-cause gloss on the deviation even though F13 supplies no incident; I therefore keep the claim confined to the strict RD-2 mileage unit rather than the full $2.33 in F4.

Conceded on the arithmetic: F1 and F3 do show one off-route segment adding 0.80 km, and I do not contest that only one segment exists — but I maintain that segment is exempt under RD-4 on the strength of F10 (AJE band 1, 0-9 km/h, 22:39-22:57) read with F11/F12/F14, since the driver was rerouting a category-1 expressway corridor that the parallel expressway was also recording at band 1.

I accept that no prior chat agreement exists (F7, F8), but RD-5 consent is not the only route to exemption — RD-4 reasonable cause is a separate and independent basis, and I rely on that instead of on agreement.

The rider's own reading of F13 is incomplete: RD-4(a) traffic incidents are only one accepted form of corroboration, and F10 is precisely the kind of road-speed record RD-4(b) contemplates, with F14 (light rain, 1.8 mm) supporting the driver's stated reason instead of contradicting it.

I do not dispute the $1.13 computation method (0.80 km × $1.41/km, F3, F4, F6); my position is only that no amount is owed if the single segment is exempt under RD-4, otherwise $1.13 is the correct and maximum figure.

The rider's own concession that the $2.33 billed excess (F4) cannot be recovered is correct under RD-2, which refunds only the unexempted segments' extra_km and expressly leaves the map-matching residual with the fare.
No waiting fee and no unpublished add-on appears in F6, so FARE-1 exposes nothing; the entire fare is the metered base, metered distance and time, plus the published platform fee.

RD-3 governs passenger-requested stops and destination changes, and none is alleged here; the applicable provision is RD-4 reasonable cause, which is met by the expressway speed-band record at F10 with the parallel-route corroboration at F11 and F12.
Agreed: F16 shows 0 of 2 disputes upheld and no route violation on the driver's record, so RD-6 flag_account is not triggered and I do not seek it.
I withdraw nothing in D2; the point stands as the correct mileage exposure (0.80 km) and it is the same figure the rider concedes in C4, so the only live issue is exemption under RD-4.
